summary: This document describes a single-page frontend application for a classroom signup service. It details the implementation of the API interaction, rendering logic, and deployment via Vercel.
key_facts: The app sends only a name to the API.
Local development uses npm install and npm run dev.
The app uses Vitest for testing, specifically for API status handling, ordinal math, and XSS escaping.
The app uses tsc --noEmit for type checking during the build process.
The app is deployed using Vercel.
The app uses Vercel auto-detection for the Vite setup.
The app uses textContent to prevent XSS attacks.

concepts.name: Dependency Injection
concepts.definition: Passing a component its collaborators as arguments instead of having it reach for globals.
concepts.in_this_source: api.ts takes fetch as an optional injected argument, which lets the tests exercise every status code without stubbing globals.

concepts.name: Vercel
concepts.definition: A cloud platform for hosting and deploying web applications.
concepts.in_this_source: The app is deployed using Vercel.

concepts.name: Vite
concepts.definition: A build tool for modern web development.
concepts.in_this_source: The app uses Vite setup and Vercel auto-detection for the Vite setup.

concepts.name: Vitest
concepts.definition: A testing framework for JavaScript/TypeScript/Web APIs.
concepts.in_this_source: The app uses Vitest for testing API status handling, ordinal math, and XSS escaping.

concepts.name: XSS Prevention
concepts.definition: Rendering untrusted input as literal text (e.g. the DOM textContent property, never innerHTML) so injected markup cannot run.
concepts.in_this_source: render.ts inserts every name with textContent because anyone can write to the endpoint; a test asserts an name renders as literal text.
